arxiv-2110-07287.title: Momentum relaxation effects in 2D-Xene field effect device structures
arxiv-2110-07287.creator: Anirban Basak, Pratik Brahma, Bhaskaran Muralidharan
arxiv-2110-07287.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Anirban Basak, Pratik Brahma, Bhaskaran Muralidharan. We analyze the electric field driven topological field effect transition on 2D-xene materials with the addition of momentum relaxation effects, in order to account for dephasing processes. The topological field effect transition between the quantum spin Hall phase and the quantum valley Hall phase is analyzed in detail using the Keldysh non-equilibrium Green’s function technique with the inclusion of momentum and phase relaxation, within the self-consistent Born approximation.

arxiv-2201-00863.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Nikhil Potu Surya Prakash Tamara Perreault Trevor Voth, Zejun Zhong. In this paper, a control algorithm for guiding a two wheeled mobile robot with unknown inertia to a desired point and orientation using an Adaptive Model Predictive Control (AMPC) framework is presented. The two wheeled mobile robot is modeled as a knife edge or a skate with nonholonomic kinematic constraints and the dynamical equations are derived using the Lagrangian approach.

arxiv-2304-02335.title: Correcting Flaws in Common Disentanglement Metrics
arxiv-2304-02335.creator: Louis Mahon, Lei Shah, Thomas Lukasiewicz
arxiv-2304-02335.description: Abstract Recent years have seen growing interest in learning disentangled representations, in which distinct features, such as size or shape, are represented by distinct neurons. Quantifying the extent to which a given representation is disentangled is not straightforward; multiple metrics have been proposed.

arxiv-2309-08075.title: Social media polarization reflects shifting political alliances in Pakistan
arxiv-2309-08075.creator: Anees Baqir, Alessandro Galeazzi, Andrea Drocco, Fabiana Zollo
arxiv-2309-08075.description: Abstract The rise of ideological divides in public discourse has received considerable attention in recent years. However, much of this research has been concentrated on Western democratic nations, leaving other regions largely unexplored. Here, we delve into the political landscape of Pakistan, a nation marked by intricate political dynamics and persistent turbulence.

pmc-10498519.title: Definitive concurrent chemoradiotherapy with docetaxel plus cisplatin versus 5-fluorouracil plus cisplatin in patients with esophageal squamous cell carcinoma: long-term follow-up results of a phase II randomized controlled trial
pmc-10498519.creator: Hui Jiang, Kanjiebubi Makelike, Baoqing Chen, Mian Xi, Qiaoqiao Li, Yonghong Hu, Yujia Zhu
pmc-10498519.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). BackgroundDefinitive radiotherapy plus concurrent chemotherapy has been a standard treatment for esophagus patients who are unfit to undergo surgery. However, there are a variety of concurrent chemotherapy regimens with varying efficacy. In this phase II prospective study, we compared the efficacy and toxicity of DP (docetaxel and cisplatin) and PF (cisplatin and 5-fluorouracil) regimens with concurrent chemoradiotherapy (CCRT) in patients with esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) and analyzed the 5-year overall survival (OS) and progression free survival (PFS).

pmc-11431344.title: Managing Virtual Presenteeism during the COVID-19 Pandemic: A Multilevel Study on Managers’ Stress Management Competencies to Foster Functional Presenteeism
pmc-11431344.creator: Sandra Salvoni, Caroline Biron, Marie-Hélène Gilbert, Julie Dextras-Gauthier, Hans Ivers, Paul B Tchounwou
pmc-11431344.description: Teleworking remains an attractive option for many workers since the COVID-19 pandemic, but it presents significant management challenges, particularly when employees face health issues. The management of virtual presenteeism, where employees continue teleworking despite being ill, has received limited attention.

pmc-11436158.title: Pfizer-BioNTech (BNT162b2) Vaccine Effectiveness against Symptomatic Laboratory-Confirmed COVID-19 Infection among Outpatients in Sentinel Sites, Lebanon, July–December 2021
pmc-11436158.creator: Lina Chaito, Pawel Stefanoff, Joaquin Baruch, Zeina Farah, Mona Albuaini, Nada Ghosn
pmc-11436158.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). On 14 February 2021, Lebanon implemented nationwide vaccination, offering the Pfizer-BioNTech (BNT162b2) vaccine to adults over 50 years of age. We estimated the effectiveness of the Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine in preventing symptomatic laboratory-confirmed COVID-19. We conducted a test-negative case–control (TND) study among symptomatic adults aged 50 years and older who presented with influenza-like illness (ILI) or COVID-19-like illness (CLI) in surveillance sentinel sites between 1 July and 31 December 2021. Unvaccinated participants did not receive any vaccine dose before symptom onset.

pmc-11512410.title: Camelpox Virus in Western Kazakhstan: Assessment of the Role of Local Fauna as Reservoirs of Infection
pmc-11512410.creator: Yerbol Bulatov, Sholpan Turyskeldy, Ruslan Abitayev, Abdurakhman Usembai, Zhanna Sametova, Zhanat Kondybayeva, Alina Kurmasheva, Dana Mazbayeva, Asselya Kyrgyzbayeva, Kamshat Shorayeva, Zhanat Amanova, Dariya Toktyrova, Yongchang Cao, Aruna Ambagala
pmc-11512410.description: This article investigates the role of local fauna in Western Kazakhstan as potential reservoirs of the camelpox virus (CMLV). The study emphasizes analyzing possible sources and transmission pathways of the virus using polymerase chain reaction (PCR) and serological methods, including virus neutralization tests and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays (ELISA).

pmc-11689208.title: ADVANCING AFFORDABLE, ACCESSIBLE HEARING CARE FOR OLDER ADULTS: FINDINGS FROM THE HEARS RCT AND ASSOCIATED STUDIES
pmc-11689208.creator: Carrie Nieman, Hae-Ra Han, Frank Lin
pmc-11689208.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Age-related hearing loss is independently associated with adverse health outcomes, but the use of hearing aids by older adults is low and disparities exist. The incorporation of community health worker (CHW)-partnered models can reduce barriers and address disparities. The HEARS (Hearing health Equity through Accessible Research & Solutions) intervention is a hearing care intervention delivered by CHWs that incorporates a low-cost amplification device and education on age-related hearing loss.

pmc-11716553.title: Cardiopulmonary coupling measures of sleep stability and risk of cognitive impairment in community‐based older men
pmc-11716553.creator: Sasha Milton, Haoqi Sun, Katie L Stone, Kristine Yaffe, Brandon Westover, Robert J Thomas, Yue Leng
pmc-11716553.description: BackgroundPoor sleep health is associated with cognitive impairment (CI) in older adults. The cardiopulmonary coupling (CPC) sleep spectrogram, which estimates the sleep state modulated synchronization between heart rate variability and respiration, is an increasingly recognized measure of sleep stability. However, little is known about the longitudinal association between CPC measures of sleep stability and risk of incident CI.

pmc-13099807.title: An insight into the experience of healthcare providers and users of women-friendly health services in Jordan—a mixed method study
pmc-13099807.creator: Eman Zmaily Dahmash, Ali Al-Gharabli, Thaira Al-Madi, Rahma Jebreel, Ahmad Shatat, Worood Al khob, Reem Al-Reyati, Wafaa Shariedeh, Walaa Shqerat, Ghada Alsaad
pmc-13099807.description: BackgroundWomen's Friendly Health Services (WFHS) are designed to be available, accessible, and affordable for women, providing care throughout their lives from youth to postmenopausal stages. These integrated services focus on women's needs, follow evidence-based practices, and are provided by a qualified and trained team.

pmc-13107375.title: Light-Induced Photomechanical Patterning of Ferroelectric Polarization
pmc-13107375.creator: Alban Degezelle, Jonas Strobelt, Sarah Loebner, Moussa Mebarki, Stéphane Fusil, Vincent Garcia, Bruno Bérini, Vincent Polewczyk, Yves Dumont, Sylvia Matzen, Philippe Lecoeur, Svetlana Santer, Thomas Maroutian
pmc-13107375.description: Tailoring at will polar textures in ferroelectrics is critical for the development of nanoscale electronics and functional oxide technologies. Freestanding ferroelectric membranes have enabled studies of strain-induced polarization responses, but the control over membrane shape and local polarization typically remains limited to spontaneous buckling or uniaxial mechanical deformations.

pmc-13141180.title: Hypothermia risk factors in patients with burns during emergency presentations: protocol for a retrospective cohort study
pmc-13141180.creator: Dhairya Deven Vayada, Maleea D Holbert, Brandon Meikle, Brett Paul Dyer, Carl Lisec, Marc Schnekenburger, Paul Baker, Monique Bertinetti, Andrew J A Holland, Roy Kimble, Anne Darton, Daniel Isacson, Varun Harish, Natalia Adanichkin, Rebecca Schrale, Linda Quinn, Bernard Carney, Bronwyn Griffin
pmc-13141180.description: IntroductionBurn injuries constitute a significant health concern, requiring immediate first aid to mitigate further tissue damage and complications. Most countries worldwide recommend application of 20 min of cool running water (20CRW) within 3 hours of the burn as the cornerstone in burn first aid management.

pmc-13421233.title: Social Vulnerability, Wildfire Exposure, and Mental Health
pmc-13421233.creator: Kyla Thomas, Evan Sandlin, Marco Angrisani, Jiyoon Kim, Margaret Gatz
pmc-13421233.description: Key PointsQuestionUnder what social conditions is wildfire exposure associated with increases in psychological distress?FindingsIn this survey study of 1510 Los Angeles County residents, conducted before and after the January 2025 wildfires, onset of wildfires was associated with a greater increase in psychological distress among evacuation zone residents compared with non–evacuation zone residents, detectable through 11 months of follow-up.

pmc-13567100.title: High Removal Rates and Atomically Smooth Surfaces Are Achieved on Silicon Wafers Using the New SiO2@ZrO2 Core–Shell Abrasive
pmc-13567100.creator: Maokui Wang, Weilong He, Kai Feng, Rui Ye, Yunci Wang, Weiyi Guan, Facheng Qiu, Xing Fan, Renlong Liu
pmc-13567100.description: The relentless miniaturization of integrated circuits demands chemical mechanical polishing (CMP) technologies that achieve both high material removal rates (MRR) and atomic-scale surface quality. Herein, we synthesize sub-100 nm SiO2@ZrO2 core–shell composite abrasives (amorphous SiO2 core ~70 nm, tetragonal ZrO2 shell ~6 nm) via a facile sol–gel method.

pmc-13630633.title: Sex-based survival disparities in patients with stage I–III non-small cell lung cancer vary by treatment modality
pmc-13630633.creator: Guus R.M. van den Heuvel, Bas L.R. Mandos, Hans J.M. Smit, Olga C.J. Schuurbiers, Erik H. J. G. Aarntzen, Iris Walraven, Francesco Ciompi, Michel M. van den Heuvel
pmc-13630633.description: IntroductionFemale sex is a well-established prognostic factor in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Most prior studies are restricted to single-treatment cohorts and seldom include best supportive care (BSC), limiting the evaluation of sex-based median overall survival across the full treatment spectrum, BSC included.

uslaw-usc-t16-s1865.title: 16 U.S.C. § 1865 — Bycatch reduction engineering program
uslaw-usc-t16-s1865.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t16-s1865.description: United States Code, Title 16 (Conservation); Chapter 38 (Fishery Conservation And Management); Subchapter IV (National Fishery Management Program). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Bycatch reduction engineering program Not later than 1 year after January 12, 2007, the Secretary, in cooperation with the Councils and other affected interests, and based upon the best scientific information available, shall establish a bycatch reduction program.
